explanation: A [[kw:promissory note]] is a written promise to repay a sum of money at a fixed future date.

explanation: A [[kw:simple discount note]] is a loan where the interest (bank discount) is deducted from the face value at the beginning.
[[kw:Bank discount]] = Face value × Discount rate × Time.
[[kw:Proceeds]] = Face value – Bank discount = amount the borrower actually receives.
Maturity value = Face value (the amount to be repaid).
[[imp:The borrower repays more than what was received; the effective interest rate is higher than the stated discount rate.]]

formulaCard.title: Effective Rate Comparison
notes: For a simple interest note, Proceeds = Face value.
For a simple discount note, Proceeds = Face value – Bank discount.

explanation: Both notes have the same face value and same dollar interest, but the proceeds and effective rates differ.
For a simple interest note: Proceeds = Face value; Effective rate = Stated rate (if time is measured in years accordingly).
For a simple discount note: Proceeds = Face value − Bank discount; Effective rate = (Bank discount ÷ Proceeds) × (360 / days).
The effective rate is always higher for a discount note because the borrower receives less money.
[[imp:Always compare effective rates, not just stated rates.]]

confusionCorner.title: Watch out!
confusionCorner.body: T-bills use a 360-day year for yield calculations, but the actual days to maturity are exact. [[imp:Always use 360 as the annual factor in the effective rate formula.]]

challengeCorner.prompt: A 270-day T-bill has a face value of $25,000 and a purchase price of $24,200. Compute effective rate (as a decimal, 4 decimals).

explanation: [[kw:Treasury bills (T-bills)]] are short-term government securities sold at a discount from face value.
They are essentially a form of simple discount note: the interest is the difference between face value and purchase price.
Effective rate for a T-bill = (Face value – Purchase price) ÷ Purchase price × (360 ÷ Days to maturity).
This gives the annualized return on the amount invested.
[[imp:T-bill effective rate is the true yield to the investor, similar to a simple discount note's effective rate.]]

formulaCard.formula: $$\text{Effective Rate} = \frac{\text{Face Value} - \text{Purchase Price}}{\text{Purchase Price}} \times \frac{360}{\text{Days to Maturity}}$$
formulaCard.title: Treasury Bill Effective Rate
notes: The interest earned is the difference between face value and purchase price.
The purchase price is analogous to proceeds in a discount note.

formulaCard.title: Blueprint for Note Problems
formulaCard.formula: $$\text{Check: } I = P \times R \times T,\ MV = P+I,\ \text{Proceeds} = P - \text{Discount}$$ $$\text{Effective Rate} = \frac{I}{\text{Proceeds}} \times \frac{360}{\text{Days}}$$

explanation: Apply the blueprint to note problems:
1. Understand: identify face value, stated rate, time, note type, and proceeds needed.
2. Solve: compute interest, proceeds, and effective rate for each option (or find missing value).
3. Conclude: compare effective rates or check that the needed cash is obtained; state the better choice.
This method prevents confusion between face value, proceeds, and maturity value.
